---
name: "1: Idea pitch"
about: One paragraph describing your intended extension, for instructor approval before real work starts
title: "Idea pitch: <your paper>, <your extension in a few words>"
labels: idea-pitch
---

## Topic and paper

- Topic: extraction, dialogue, grounding, memory, or evaluation.
- Paper: title, authors, year, arXiv ID or link. Note whether it is from
  the course's own curated menu or self-proposed.
- Repo you are building the baseline from (link), or, if there is none,
  say so plainly here, this changes how much work the baseline issue is.

## The limitation you are extending

One paragraph. What specific gap, weakness, or unanswered question in the
baseline paper does your extension target. Not "make it better" or "add
an LLM," a real, specific limitation the paper itself either states or
that you can point to concretely.

## Your extension idea

One paragraph. What you will actually build or change, and why it
addresses the limitation above.

## Related work check

Have you searched for a published follow-up paper on this same baseline
that already does something close to your idea? List what you found, even
if the answer is "nothing found." This is the one thing this issue exists
to catch, silence on this point is itself a flag when the report is
graded later.

## Compute and cost cap check

State plainly: does this run on a personal computer, or fit inside $20 of
total API spend. If a smoke test will stand in for full-scale validation,
say so now, not after the work is done.

## Approval

- [ ] Instructor has read and approved this pitch (comment below with
  approval or requested changes)

Do not start real baseline or extension work until this is checked off.
